title: Add reusable zero-allocation animation pose buffer
description:
## Summary
Introduce a reusable indexed mutable pose buffer for high-frequency animation frames so animation does not allocate a complete immutable PosedSkeleton/Vector3 array on every tick. The buffer is an implementation mechanism, not a replacement for immutable pose snapshots.

## Audit provenance
Synthesized from CCANIM-20260908-ROADMAP-4F2C9A71 A2 and reconciled with TSK-0134's existing steady-state performance ownership.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One reusable pose buffer can hold indexed position and rotation data for a creature's skeleton.
- Initialization validates skeleton identity/count and rejects incompatible or nonfinite data.
- Per-frame sampling/application performs no managed allocations after warmup.
- Rest-pose reset/copy semantics are explicit and tested.
- Applying a buffer does not regenerate geometry, recalculate weights, resolve semantic IDs, or rebuild the renderer.
- Existing immutable PosedSkeleton behavior remains compatible for snapshot/interchange callers.
- Add focused runtime tests covering reuse, compatibility, malformed lengths, nonfinite values, rest reset, and allocation-free repeated application where the existing test harness permits it.

## Validation
.NET build/tests and diff review are required. Authoritative zero-allocation renderer/frame evidence belongs to TSK-0134 and requires Unity PlayMode/profiling; do not claim it here without Unity execution.

## Dependencies
TSK-0188, TSK-0118, TSK-0132, TSK-0133, TSK-0134.

## Scope boundary
Do not add clip playback, locomotion, blending policy, Animator/Avatar integration, or speculative pooling infrastructure. Keep ownership explicit: one buffer per animated creature unless a later measured requirement justifies another strategy.
